mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point increase in unemployment rate over three months signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns within five trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE increases by over 0.5pp in three months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and industrial production indicate broad economic weakness in consumer demand and manufacturing output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO decline by over 1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a federal funds rate increase signals aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises by over 0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) consistently signal strong consumer demand for housing, boosting construction activity and consumer confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payrolls exceeding 200,000 monthly indicate a robust labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns within five trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate demand-pull inflation that triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS rises by over 0.5% and CPIAUCSL rises by over 0.2% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100.5 signals manufacturing contraction that reduces business investment and output capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days in a slowdown regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.5.
